This is my cycle-2 fix 1, applied. Each claim is checked. (1) Hesiod's Theogony has Atlas 'uphold the wide heaven' (Theoi), and he is a Titan, son of Iapetus. (2) Later tellings made him a king of Mauretania 'skilled in philosophy, mathematics, and astronomy' (Wikipedia, Atlas (mythology)), which fits 'wise king … who studied the stars'. (3) Mercator chose the title in that king's honour; his preface sets 'this man Atlas, so notable for his erudition, humaneness, and wisdom' as his model (Wikipedia, Mercator). (4) Mercator died in Duisburg on 2 December 1594 (Britannica). The Library of Congress says the work was 'left unfinished … edited and published by his son, Rumold Mercator, in 1595'. 'It came out in 1595, the year after he died' is right; parts had appeared from 1585, but not under the name Atlas. (5) Wikipedia (Atlas): from the mid-17th century the word meant simply a collection of maps; M-W: 'a bound collection of maps'. M-W's 'Did you know' gives the other account, a picture of Atlas on the title page. The card does not assert that account, so nothing on it is false. The eponyms file still asserts it (owner question).
